key_insight: Data-free PINNs capture velocity in a deep lid-driven cavity, but accuracy varies by region and observable, with substantial rotational-field discrepancies remaining.
engineering_relevance: Deep-cavity flow predictions need regional validation because bulk velocity agreement can obscure errors in weak recirculation far below the lid.
method: Hard-constrained streamfunction PINNs for steady 2D incompressible flow at depth-to-width ratio 5 and Re = 100–1000.
Prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants.
Validation against independent spectral/hp reference fields using the same Gaussian-regularized lid.
evidence_signal: On a 121×605 grid, interior relative velocity discrepancies were 5.130–7.850% and floor-region discrepancies stayed below 5%; a separate 161×801 evaluation at Re = 1000 showed refinement reducing interior discrepancy from 5.624% to 2.658%.
watch_item: Improvements compare accumulated training workflows rather than isolating regional sampling, and configuration rankings depend on region and observable.
paper_title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
